catalogTopics.method: Question-part review against current CED; original scan checked

candidates.name: Integrated rate laws and half-life
candidates.definition: Using concentration-versus-time relationships for zero, first and second order reactions, linear plots ([A], ln[A], 1/[A] versus time), rate constants from slopes, and first-order half-life.
candidates.include: Tag when concentration at a time, half-life, or order from a linear plot must be determined.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag initial-rate tables (tag rate-law).

candidates.name: Molecular geometry (VSEPR)
candidates.definition: Predicting electron-domain geometry and molecular shape from the arrangement of bonding and lone-pair domains around a central atom.
candidates.include: Tag when a molecular or electron-domain geometry must be named, identified, drawn or used.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag hybridization-only questions (tag hybridization) or bond-angle questions where shape is given (tag bond-angles).

candidates.name: Rate laws and reaction order
candidates.definition: Determining reaction orders, the overall order, the rate constant and its units from experimental data, typically initial rates, and predicting rate changes when concentrations change.
candidates.include: Tag when orders, a rate law, k, or a predicted rate change must be determined.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag mechanism-based rate-law derivation (tag mechanism-rate-law) or integrated-rate-law graphs (tag integrated-rate-laws).

candidates.name: Electron-domain counting
candidates.definition: Counting the electron domains around a central atom, where each lone pair and each bond (single, double or triple) counts as one domain.
candidates.include: Tag when the answer depends on counting domains, including the rule that a multiple bond is one domain, as a supporting step for geometry or hybridization.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag when geometry or hybridization is simply recalled for a familiar molecule without domain reasoning being needed.

candidates.name: Resonance and delocalization
candidates.definition: Representing a species with two or more valid Lewis structures, understanding the real structure as a hybrid with delocalized electrons, and the resulting equal or fractional bond orders.
candidates.include: Tag when resonance structures must be drawn or identified, or when delocalization explains equal bond lengths or stability.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag isomers (different atom connections) or a single Lewis structure with no alternative arrangement.

candidates.name: Orbital hybridization
candidates.definition: Assigning sp, sp2 or sp3 hybridization to an atom from its number of electron domains.
candidates.include: Tag when the hybridization of an atom must be stated or used.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag geometry-only answers; d-orbital hybridization, drawing hybrid orbitals and molecular-orbital diagrams are not assessed.

candidates.name: Lewis structures
candidates.definition: Drawing or interpreting Lewis electron-dot diagrams: counting total valence electrons, placing bonding and lone pairs, multiple bonds, octet exceptions and polyatomic-ion charges.
candidates.include: Tag when the student must draw a Lewis structure, or must determine bonding and lone pairs that are not shown in order to answer.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag when a complete Lewis structure is given and is only read for a later step that is tagged separately, unless reading it requires electron counting.

candidates.name: Reaction rates
candidates.definition: Defining and determining average and instantaneous rates from concentration-time data, and relating rates of reactant loss and product formation through stoichiometry.
candidates.include: Tag when a rate must be calculated from data or slopes, or rates of different species related.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag rate-law or order determination (tag rate-law).

candidates.name: Bond angles
candidates.definition: Predicting or comparing bond angles from electron-domain geometry, including the compression caused by lone pairs.
candidates.include: Tag when a bond angle must be estimated, compared or explained.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag when only a shape name is requested.

candidates.name: Formal charge
candidates.definition: Calculating the formal charge on atoms in a Lewis structure and using formal charges to judge which of several structures best represents a species.
candidates.include: Tag when formal charges must be calculated, compared, or used to choose the preferred structure, even if the words 'formal charge' do not appear.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag oxidation numbers (tag oxidation-numbers) or a Lewis structure question whose answer does not depend on formal charge.

candidates.name: Molecular polarity
candidates.definition: Deciding whether a molecule has a net dipole from its bond dipoles and three-dimensional shape.
candidates.include: Tag when the student must determine or justify whether a molecule is polar or nonpolar.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag when polarity is stated in the question and only used to compare forces (tag the specific force).

candidates.name: Sigma and pi bonds
candidates.definition: Counting sigma and pi bonds in single, double and triple bonds and explaining restricted rotation about double bonds.
candidates.include: Tag when sigma and pi bonds must be counted or distinguished, or rotation about a bond is explained.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag simple bond-order comparisons (tag bond-order).

candidates.name: Bond enthalpies
candidates.definition: Estimating ΔH of a reaction as the energy of bonds broken minus the energy of bonds formed, and explaining energy changes as bond breaking (endothermic) and formation (exothermic).
candidates.include: Tag when average bond enthalpies are used to estimate ΔH, or bonds broken and formed must be counted.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag bond-length comparisons (tag bond-order).

candidates.name: Bond order, length and strength
candidates.definition: Relating the number of shared electron pairs between two atoms (including fractional bond orders from resonance) to bond length and bond strength.
candidates.include: Tag when bond lengths or bond strengths are compared or explained from single, double, triple or resonance-averaged bonds.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag when bonds are only counted for a bond-enthalpy calculation (tag bond-enthalpy).

candidates.name: Bond polarity and partial charges
candidates.definition: Using electronegativity difference to decide whether a bond is polar, the direction of its dipole, and which atom carries the partial negative charge.
candidates.include: Tag when bond dipoles or partial charges on bonded atoms must be identified or compared.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag whole-molecule polarity questions unless individual bond dipoles are explicitly reasoned about (tag molecular-polarity).

candidates.name: Molarity and solution preparation
candidates.definition: Calculating and using molar concentration (moles of solute per liter of solution), including preparing a solution of a target concentration.
candidates.include: Tag when molarity must be calculated, or moles found from molarity and volume as a substantive step.
candidates.exclude: Molality and percent-by-mass concentrations are not assessed (tag colligative-properties if present); dilution belongs to dilution.

candidates.name: Bond potential-energy curves
candidates.definition: Interpreting the potential energy of two atoms as a function of distance: equilibrium bond length at the energy minimum, bond energy as the well depth, and the attractive and repulsive forces that shape the curve.
candidates.include: Tag when a potential-energy versus internuclear-distance graph is read, drawn or explained.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag bond-length or bond-strength comparisons that do not involve the energy curve (tag bond-order).

candidates.name: Dipole-dipole attractions
candidates.definition: Attractions between the permanent dipoles of polar molecules.
candidates.include: Tag when dipole-dipole forces must be identified or compared.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag hydrogen bonding cases unless the comparison involves dipole-dipole forces specifically.

candidates.name: Enthalpy of reaction
candidates.definition: The enthalpy change of a reaction as written, its sign, and how it scales with the amount reacting in a thermochemical equation.
candidates.include: Tag when heat released or absorbed must be calculated from ΔH and an amount of reactant, or ΔH related to a balanced equation.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag bond-enthalpy, formation-enthalpy or Hess's-law calculations unless ΔH scaling to an amount is also required.

candidates.name: Molecular structure and acid strength
candidates.definition: Explaining relative acid strength from bond polarity and strength, electronegativity of nearby atoms (oxyacids, inductive effects), and stabilization of the conjugate base by resonance or charge.
candidates.include: Tag when acid strengths must be ranked or explained from molecular structure.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag strength ranking from given Ka values only (tag weak-acid-equilibrium).

candidates.name: Beer-Lambert law and spectrophotometry
candidates.definition: Using A = εbc and calibration curves to relate absorbance to concentration, choosing a wavelength, and evaluating spectrophotometry procedures.
candidates.include: Tag when absorbance data, a calibration curve or the Beer-Lambert relationship must be used.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag general spectroscopy questions without an absorbance-concentration relationship.

candidates.name: Nuclear chemistry
candidates.definition: Radioactive decay modes, nuclear equations and nuclear binding energy. Not assessed on the current AP Chemistry exam (first-order half-life math belongs to integrated-rate-laws).
candidates.include: Tag legacy questions about decay particles, nuclear equations or transmutation.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag first-order kinetics problems that merely use radioactive decay as context unless nuclear equations are required.

candidates.name: Mechanisms and rate laws
candidates.definition: Deriving the rate law predicted by a mechanism from its slow step, including fast pre-equilibrium steps that eliminate intermediates, and testing mechanisms against experimental rate laws.
candidates.include: Tag when a rate law must be derived from a mechanism, or a mechanism judged consistent with an observed rate law.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag experimental order determination with no mechanism.

candidates.name: Oxidation numbers
candidates.definition: Assigning oxidation numbers to atoms and using changes in oxidation number to identify which species are oxidized and reduced and how many electrons transfer.
candidates.include: Tag when oxidation numbers must be assigned or changes in them used.
candidates.exclude: Terms 'oxidizing agent' and 'reducing agent' are not assessed on the current exam; do not confuse with formal charge.
